summary: Normalize now takes out hiss, hum, fan and room tone before it raises the level, so a quiet recording comes up without its noise coming up with it. It is on by default, runs on this Mac, and is a setting on the segment you can change or remove.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open Scripts/playtest/fixtures/Noisy voice recording 1280x800.mp4 (walk: normalize-cleans-noise-walk).

try.do: Open the noisy recording and click its clip on the timeline. Under Gain, Clean noise is already checked beside Normalize.
Uncheck Clean noise and press Normalize: +29.5 dB, and the noise between the words fills the lane.
Press Cmd-Z, check Clean noise, press Normalize: a ring fills on the segment, then +30.7 dB with a sparkle, flat pauses, and a Noise row at Medium.
Press space and listen to a pause, then drag the Noise slider to Strong and to Light.
Right-click the segment: Normalize has Clean Noise checked inside it, and Remove Noise Cleaning sits below it.
Press the x at the end of the Noise row: the row goes, the gain stays, the noise is back. Cmd-Z brings it back.
Play queue/audits/2026-09-29-clean-noise-ab.m4a: ten seconds normalized alone, a short gap, then the same ten seconds normalized with Clean noise.

evaluate: On one of your own recordings, does Medium take the fan or room tone out without the voice sounding watery or swallowed at the ends of words?
Is Clean noise under the Normalize button the right place, or would you rather find the strength in a sound Effects list as the mock draws it?
Does the sparkle on the segment tell you the sound is cleaned, or is it too small to notice?
Should Clean noise also be offered on its own when a recording is added, without Normalize?
rough: Measured on the fixture: noise floor after Normalize alone -25.3 dBFS, after Normalize with Clean noise -44.1 dBFS (18.8 dB lower); the voice within 0.5 dB (-17.9 against -18.4 dBFS RMS over the spoken windows).

The fixture is not a microphone recording: it is macOS speech mixed with fan-band noise and a 60 Hz hum, because this Mac gave the loop no microphone. Judge it on a real recording of yours before trusting it.
The mock puts Noise reduction in the sound's Effects menu (video-audio.html, efxMenu). Sound has no Effects group yet, so the strength lives on a Noise row under Gain for now.
The acceptance asked for Clean noise beside Normalize; the panel column is too narrow for both on one line, so it sits directly under the button.
On a recording with no noise at all, cleaning still learns from its quietest moments and changes loudness slightly: the quiet test tone's Loudness for Web gain moved from +28.7 to +28.3 dB.

The ring on the segment while a copy is being made was not photographed: on a ten second clip the copy is ready in well under a second. A playthrough that is under way restarts on the cleaned sound when it lands; that was built but not heard in a walk.
